evidence.VOTE: On 18 December 2017 at the Security Council's 8139th meeting, the Egypt-submitted draft S/2017/1060 received 14 votes in favour and one against. The United States cast the sole negative vote. The Council did not adopt the text because a permanent member voted against.
evidence.TEXT: The draft addressed measures purporting to alter Jerusalem's status and called upon states to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. These were provisions of the draft.
evidence.US-A: Nikki Haley framed the United States no vote as defending its authority to decide the location of its embassy.
evidence.US-B: Haley rejected the claim that United States recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital harmed the peace process and affirmed continued United States commitment to peace.
evidence.UK-A: Matthew Rycroft said the United Kingdom supported the draft as consistent with previous Council resolutions and its longstanding position. He disagreed with unilateral recognition before a final status agreement and with moving the United States embassy.
evidence.UK-B: Rycroft said the city's status should be determined through negotiations between Israelis and Palestinians and supported Jerusalem as the eventual shared capital of the two states.

criteria.A1: Accurately identifies what the draft would have said about measures altering the city's status.
criteria.A2: Reports the diplomatic-mission provision as proposed wording.
criteria.P1: Preserves the United States objection about authority over embassy location.
criteria.P2: Preserves the United Kingdom's support for the draft and its negotiated-status position.
criteria.C1: Recognizes the stated desire for peace without claiming agreement on Jerusalem.
criteria.C2: Records the concrete dispute about unilateral recognition or the embassy move.
criteria.S1: Does not convert the draft or the affirmative majority into an adopted Council mandate.
criteria.S2: Does not say that the vote determined sovereignty or an agreed final status.
